input.title: Choose where to store carts: Redis or Postgres
input.body:
Simply put: the cookie holds only a cart ID, and the cart contents live server-side, so long carts no longer hit the 4 KB limit.

**Redis**: very fast, and a TTL expires abandoned carts automatically. It is an extra service to run unless you already have it. Data is in memory, so you need persistence configured or accept losing carts on a restart.

**Postgres**: carts are durable and transactional, and you can query them (abandoned-cart reports, support lookups). It is likely already in your stack. Writes add load to the main database, and you need a cleanup job for old carts.

**My pick: Postgres**, unless you already run Redis with persistence. Cart data is business data, and one fewer service to operate outweighs the speed difference at typical cart volumes.

content.text:
A1 [open] decision: Choose where to store carts: Redis or Postgres
actions: a1 resolve "Use Postgres", a2 resolve "Use Redis"
